claims.text: Airbags failed to deploy during collisions in two separate incidents.
The driver's seatbelt failed to lock during a rear-end impact.
Restraint failures occurred during crashes resulting in injuries.

report.summary: Three complaints for the 2015 model year report restraint system failures during crashes, including non-deployment of airbags and failure of the seatbelt to lock. These incidents resulted in injuries and significant vehicle damage. The failures are distinct from previous Takata recalls which focused on inflator ruptures rather than non-deployment.
report.rationale: The evidence is severe but thin and inconsistent. The complaints describe different failure modes (non-deployment vs. seatbelt locking failure), making it difficult to identify a single specific defect for engineering review at this time. However, the severity of the incidents warrants continued monitoring.
report.failure_mode: non-deployment of airbags and seatbelt locking failure

claims.text: One 2019 vehicle experienced a total brake failure to engage during a sudden stop, resulting in a rear-end collision.
One 2019 vehicle reported the brake pedal gradually sinking to the floor over several weeks, reducing stopping confidence.
One 2019 vehicle reported low voltage issues and a parking brake that would not turn off.

report.summary: Three complaints were identified for the 2019 model year regarding braking issues, but they describe unrelated failure modes. These include a sudden failure to engage leading to a crash, a gradual increase in pedal travel to the floor, and an electrical issue affecting the parking brake.
report.rationale: The complaints for the 2019 model year are too few and describe completely different failure modes (sudden failure, soft pedal, and electrical/parking brake), indicating no consistent defect for an engineer to review.

claims.text: The liftgate or tailgate opened spontaneously while the vehicle was being driven at various speeds.
One instance of spontaneous opening occurred at approximately 60 mph on a highway, making the vehicle hard to control.
Spontaneous opening of the tailgate resulted in contents falling out of the vehicle while driving up a hill.
The liftgate has also been reported to open on its own while the vehicle was parked and locked.
The reported failures are concentrated in the 2019 model year.

report.summary: Multiple reports indicate that the liftgate/tailgate of the 2019 [VEHICLE] opens spontaneously while the vehicle is in motion. This has occurred at highway speeds and resulted in cargo falling onto the roadway. No existing recalls address this specific failure mode.
report.rationale: There is a consistent failure mode of the liftgate opening spontaneously during vehicle operation, which creates a significant safety risk to the driver and other road users. This is not covered by any of the provided recalls.
report.failure_mode: spontaneous opening of the liftgate/tailgate while driving

claims.text: Vehicles experience violent shaking of the steering wheel and front end, referred to as 'death wobble', typically at speeds between 45 and 75 mph.
The oscillation is frequently triggered by hitting a bump, pothole, or expansion joint while driving straight.
Drivers must apply brakes and reduce speed significantly (often below 40 mph) to stop the shaking and regain control.
The defect has been diagnosed as worn track bar ball joints and bushings.
Replacing the steering stabilizer shock is reported as an ineffective fix for the underlying problem.
The issue has caused near-loss of vehicle control and dangerous situations on highways.
The problem is reported across multiple model years, including 2015, 2016, and 2017.

report.summary: Multiple consumers report a violent front-end oscillation known as 'death wobble' occurring at highway speeds, often triggered by road bumps. The condition causes severe steering instability and requires significant deceleration to regain control. Evidence suggests the issue is linked to worn track bar ball joints and bushings.
report.rationale: There is a consistent, specific failure mode (death wobble) with high safety severity (near-loss of control at highway speeds) and a suspected root cause (track bar ball joints). This is not addressed by any existing recalls.
report.failure_mode: Violent steering and front-end oscillation ('death wobble') triggered by road bumps at highway speeds, linked to track bar ball joint/bushing wear.

claims.text: Consumers report that dealerships are unable to replace defective Takata airbags due to part unavailability.
Owners express safety concerns and fear of fatality because the known airbag recall has not been repaired.
One owner reported receiving airbag warning lights for both driver and passenger sides, which they associated with the unresolved recall.
Part availability issues for the Takata recall are reported across multiple model years, including 2010, 2011, and 2012.

report.summary: The recent spike in complaints for the 2012 [VEHICLE] is driven by consumer frustration regarding the lack of replacement parts for existing Takata airbag recalls. There is no evidence of a new failure mode; rather, owners are reporting that dealerships cannot perform the mandated safety repairs.
report.rationale: The complaints do not describe a new defect but rather the failure to execute existing recalls (19V010000, 17V017000). The issue is a matter of remedy availability for a known hazard already covered by previous recall campaigns.
report.failure_mode: Lack of remedy parts for existing Takata airbag recalls

A 2013 vehicle reported a total engine failure after a recall was completed.
Other model years report unrelated acceleration issues, including pedal interference (2013) and throttle body failure (2010).

report.summary: The investigation examined a signal of unintended acceleration for the 2013 [VEHICLE]. The complaints are inconsistent, with one reporting sudden acceleration, one reporting independent brake engagement followed by engine failure, and one reporting a general engine blowout.
report.rationale: The complaints for the 2013 model year are unrelated and do not describe a consistent failure mode. One is a severe acceleration event, while the others are engine failures. Broader data shows a mix of unrelated causes for acceleration issues across different years.

claims.text: 2020 EcoDiesel vehicles exhibit a delay of several seconds between pressing the accelerator and the vehicle responding, often during turns or merging.
The delay is often followed by a sudden burst of power or surge in acceleration.
Owners of 2014-2016 EcoDiesel models report that this throttle lag appeared specifically after an EPA-mandated emissions software update (AEM V08).
The condition is reported to be more prevalent or severe when the engine is cold.
The lag creates a safety hazard when attempting to cross traffic or merge into lanes.

report.summary: Multiple consumers report a dangerous delay in throttle response in EcoDiesel vehicles, where the engine fails to accelerate for several seconds before suddenly surging. This issue is reported across several model years and is specifically linked by some users to emissions software updates. The hazard is misclassified as unintended acceleration but is actually a loss of propulsion/acceleration lag.
report.rationale: There is a consistent, specific failure mode (throttle lag) across multiple model years of the EcoDiesel engine that creates a significant safety risk during critical driving maneuvers. This is not covered by any existing recalls.
report.failure_mode: Significant throttle response lag/delay followed by sudden acceleration in EcoDiesel engines.

claims.text: The right rear passenger speaker frequently melts, producing a burning smell and smoke inside the vehicle.
Failures are often preceded by crackling or rattling noises coming from the speaker.
Smoke filling the cabin has caused drivers to believe the vehicle was on fire and pull over.
One dealer identified a faulty amplifier as the cause of the speaker melting.
The issue has been reported to occur even when the radio is turned off.
A separate incident involved burned installation and melted wiring due to a missing emissions bolt.

report.summary: Multiple 2014 vehicles exhibit a consistent failure where the audio speakers, particularly the right rear passenger speaker, melt and emit smoke and burning odors. This issue is often preceded by crackling or rattling noises and may be linked to a faulty amplifier. No existing recall addresses this electrical failure.
report.rationale: There is a highly consistent failure mode involving melting speakers and smoke in the cabin for the 2014 model year. This represents a fire hazard and a safety risk to occupants, and it is not covered by any of the listed recalls.
report.failure_mode: Audio speaker (primarily right rear) melts, causing smoke and burning odors in the cabin, potentially due to a faulty amplifier.

claims.text: One vehicle experienced unintended side airbag deployment during a tire blowout at speeds under 10mph without a crash.
Multiple vehicles from the 2008 model year report airbag warning lights or sensor failures.
A consumer reported difficulty obtaining parts for a previously announced airbag recall.
Several model years exhibit dashboard cracking in the area of the passenger airbag, raising concerns about debris during deployment.

report.summary: The signal consists of three unrelated complaints: one reporting unintended side airbag deployment during a tire blowout, one reporting a warning light, and one regarding the unavailability of parts for a previous recall. Other complaints for this vehicle show a pattern of dashboard cracking and generic airbag sensor failures, but no single consistent defect is evident.
report.rationale: The complaints in the signal do not describe a consistent failure mode. One is an isolated incident of unintended deployment, one is a generic warning light, and one is a complaint about recall execution. While dashboard cracking is a recurring theme in the broader data, it is not the primary signal and does not constitute a consistent airbag system failure.
